styles.label: Temples
styles.blurb: Grand Palace, Wat Pho and the river temples.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Street stalls, markets and Chinatown nights.

stays.why: On the BTS Skytrain and MRT, endless food and nightlife, easy airport link. Good first-time base.
Central shopping malls and the Skytrain interchange; short rides to most sights.
River views, express boats to the temples and ICONSIAM; quieter evenings.
Walk to the Grand Palace and Wat Pho; cheapest beds and the backpacker strip.

food: Eat street food where locals queue: noodles, grilled chicken and som tam for roughly ฿50–120 a plate.
Yaowarat (Chinatown) after dark is the classic food crawl; go hungry and share dishes.
Try the big local dishes: boat noodles, pad thai, khao soi and mango sticky rice.
Food courts in malls are cheap, clean and air-conditioned; a good rainy-day option.
Drink bottled or filtered water; ice in busy cafés and stalls is usually fine, but use your judgement.
more_time: Swap a temple day for a day trip to Ayutthaya by train or minivan; ruins and history, check times on the day.
Add a floating market or canal trip outside the centre; go early morning to beat the heat and crowds.
Spend a night in Chinatown for food and markets, or take a cooking class to learn the dishes you liked.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the river temples, Chinatown food and a mall or market day without rushing in the heat.

month_notes: Jan: coolest and driest month, highs near 31°C. Great for walking the temples.
Feb: warm and dry, about 5 rain days. Comfortable for sightseeing.
Mar: hotter at 33°C and more rain days. Start early and rest at midday.
Apr: hottest month, 34°C highs. Plan indoor breaks and drink lots of water.
May: wet season starts, around 20 rain days. Carry a light rain jacket.
Jun: rainy, about 23 rain days. Short heavy showers; keep plans flexible.
Jul: wet and warm, 24 rain days. Malls and food courts are good backups.
Aug: one of the wettest months, 26 rain days. Expect afternoon downpours.
Sep: still very wet, 26 rain days. Watch for flooded streets after storms.
Oct: rain eases a little, 22 rain days. Late month is usually better.
Nov: drier and cooler, about 11 rain days. A good shoulder month.
Dec: cool and dry, around 4 rain days. One of the best months to visit.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical city: hot all year, with a dry, cooler season from November to February and a long wet season from May to October.

items.title: Best time: November to February
items.text: Highs around 31–32°C, lows 22–23°C and only 4–5 rain days. Best for temples and walking.

items.title: Hot season: March to May
items.text: Highs of 33–34°C. Sightsee early morning and late afternoon; rest in air-conditioning at midday.

items.title: Wet season: May to October
items.text: 20–26 rain days a month, often short heavy afternoon showers. Carry a light rain jacket or umbrella.

items.title: Humid all year
items.text: Expect sticky air most days. Light, breathable clothes help; so does a spare shirt.

items.title: Plan around the rain
items.text: Keep indoor backups like malls, food courts and museums. Storms usually pass within an hour or two.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, sandals, sunscreen and a hat. Cover shoulders and knees for temples. A rain jacket for May–October.

transit.best: BTS Skytrain and MRT for the centre, river boats for temples, and Grab or Bolt for the rest.

modes.text: BTS Skytrain and MRT subway cover the centre; fares about ฿16–65, contactless cards accepted on most lines.
City buses are very cheap but hard to use for visitors.
Metered taxis start at ฿35; insist on the meter. Grab and Bolt apps are often easier.
Not recommended for visitors: heavy traffic and hard parking. Use trains, boats and apps instead.
Walking is hot and pavements are uneven; combine short walks with the Skytrain.
Chao Phraya Express boats link the riverside temples, Chinatown and ICONSIAM.
Tuk-tuks are fun for short rides; agree the price first.
